# uptimeify_package_config (Resource)

One package of the organization, addressed by its `package_type` (`PATCH /api/package-configs/{packageType}`). Manages the limits only: monitors, status pages and self-service per customer of the package. The check and alert defaults of the package stay as they are (the server's defaults for a new package); read them with `data.uptimeify_package_configs`. If the package already exists, creating the resource adopts it. Destroy deletes the package and fails (`packageInUse`) while customers use it. Import with the package type.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "uptimeify_package_config" "business" {
  package_type       = "business"
  display_name       = "Business"
  max_urls           = 50
  max_status_pages   = 3 # unset = unlimited
  allow_self_service = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `package_type` (String) Package key, 1 to 64 characters, no surrounding whitespace, e.g. `essential`. Changing it replaces the package.

### Optional

- `allow_self_service` (Boolean) Customers of the package may create their own (`self_service`) monitors and status pages. Unset = kept as is.
- `display_name` (String) Name shown in the UI, 1 to 64 characters. Unset = kept as is.
- `max_self_service_urls` (Number) Self-service monitors per customer. Unset = kept as is.
- `max_status_pages` (Number) Status pages per customer of this package. Unset = unlimited. Pages without a customer never count.
- `max_urls` (Number) Monitors per customer. Unset = kept as is (a new package uses the default of its type).
- `notes` (String) Internal notes, up to 4096 characters. Unset = kept as is (the API cannot clear them).

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Same as `package_type`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Package type
terraform import uptimeify_package_config.business business
```
